text: The Department of Natural Resources said on Tuesday that drilling at the Hadrow Flats survey site in eastern Merrow has confirmed a substantial potash deposit beneath the salt plain. In a briefing note filed with Parliament’s geology committee and obtained by The Continental Record, chief surveyor Elin Voss said core samples taken from three boreholes between May 14 and June 2 showed “commercially significant potash-bearing seams” at depths of 310 to 460 metres. The department estimated the deposit at 18.4 million tonnes, though it cautioned that further assay work is needed before any mining licence is considered. Local officials in Bracken Ward said they would review water and transport impacts next month.
